scope: Static native and serialized-asset reconstruction only. No game, Unity editor play mode, client, server, listening socket or connection/protocol test was run for this audit.
conclusion: In the modern OnConnected avatar-loaded path, the client places its local NebulaPlayer at one of six Nexus ManagerInstance.spawnPoints and copies its forward vector before revealing the scene. Earlier transport/preset coordinates do not determine the final arrival position in this path.

confidence.native_path: direct bounded x64 instructions and Ghidra pseudocode
confidence.coordinates: parsed serialized Unity Transform trees and identity prefab root; not observed runtime coordinates
confidence.global_behavior: bounded initial-load path; not a proof about later gameplay teleports, scene edits, collision settling or all modes

loading.finding: Builds s/ + Scenes.Active + logicprefab, then awaits NebulaAssetBundleManager.Load. For Active=nexus this is s/nexuslogicprefab; it does not use s/pre/nexuslogicprefab.
Loads dependencies, resolves StreamingAssets/platform/relativePath, loads bundle and all assets asynchronously, returns request.asset. This stage does not instantiate or place the prefab.

After await LoadLogicPrefab, calls the one-argument Object.Instantiate<GameObject>(asset) overload at 0x8953d0, without parent/position/rotation parameters; no transform setter occurs in this body. Loads optional event prefab, destroys loading camera/ScreenLoader, then calls ManagerInstance.Launch at 0x46feaf.

Calls TCPInit; initializes cinema and optional night cycle. Does not replace spawnPoints. Bounded scans of 54 ManagerInstance/ManagerInstanceNexus methods find no memory operand displacement 0x160; this is scoped negative evidence, not a global field-use proof.

steps.action: UnityEngine.Random.Range(int 0, array.Length) chooses one element. No saved-position or server-coordinate field is read in this selection.
Assign that position to the local NebulaPlayer Transform.
Assign that forward vector to local NebulaPlayer Transform.forward.
Set local player Animator bool AnimInfinite to false.
Align NebulaCamManager.cameraPivotY X/Z to spawn; its Y is PlayerLabel.targetCam Transform.position.y minus float 0.45. This is a separate transform from the avatar root.
Store coroutine state 1 and yield null for one frame.
Resumed state hides ScreenLoader; then clears ManagerInstance.isChatMenuLocked at offset 0x272.

native_placement.selection: Random.Range(0,6); client RNG state is not recovered, so no single spawn index can be predicted statically.

ordering: Scene logic prefab is loaded and instantiated before ManagerInstance.Launch initializes/connects networking.

CreatePlayer(0x5f6a80) -> CREATEPLAYER.MoveNext(0x6033e0) instantiates the gender base, then CreateGhost(0x5f63e0) applies AvatarInfo.lastPos to the NebulaPlayer root for both local and remote avatars.

Asset assembly completes through PostInstantiateAssets(0x5fc840) and End(0x5f6ef0); CREATEPLAYER.MoveNext then clears loading flags and invokes NebulaPlayerAvatar.OnAvatarLoaded(+0xf8) with NebulaPlayer.GUID(+0xa0).
OnConnectedProcessor avatar-loading continuation calls OnAvatarLoaded at 0x5dfdc0.
OnAvatarLoaded initializes local control/random idle, sends its stored application opcode 1 through TCPClient.Send, then constructs MoveAvatarDelay state 0 and starts it on the local NebulaPlayer.
MoveAvatarDelay state 0 sets avatar position/forward to a chosen scene point, then yields null. State1 hides the loading screen and unlocks chat menu.

saved_position.finding: HTTPGetPresetGame.OnResponse(0x622740) parses LastPosJson xyz and passes that Vector3 into AvatarInfo.ctor(0x605d40). AvatarInfo.lastPos is actually applied early by NebulaPlayerAvatar.CreateGhost(0x5f63e0): param_2 is NebulaPlayer, param_3 is AvatarInfo; it copies AvatarInfo+0x60/+0x68 into a Vector3 and calls Transform.set_position. Both local and remote paths converge before this assignment; isLocal at+0x9c only gates the earlier PS4Info.gender update. The reviewed later MoveAvatarDelay never reads LastPos; it supersedes this initial position for the local player. Remote avatars retain the initial HTTP position until other movement updates.
saved_position.cross_audit: Exact earlier application/order supplied by the avatar agent from its existing static audit; original source files are hashed below.
saved_position.not_claimed: This does not claim LastPos is unused by remote-avatar construction, wardrobes, persistence, personal spaces, alternate paths or later teleports.

server_implications: Do not claim Mirror initial position(0,0,0) is a verified safe/visible Nexus arrival point. The client later moves its own root to a scene spawn before ScreenLoader.Hide.
The C2S opcode 1 send precedes this final local placement and carries no chosen spawn index or coordinates in the recovered application message.

Preserving this client behavior requires the real scene logic prefab, valid local player/control/camera/label components and completion of avatar load. Sending only an HTTP LastPos or Mirror position cannot replace those initialization steps.
Server ownership and later NetworkTransform replication are a separate Mirror contract. This static spawn audit does not establish a successful connection or a working world session.
known_limits: No assertion about collider settling after the one-frame yield.
No full global proof that another component cannot later move the prefab/player.
No original server code or original server spawn policy was recovered.
No target runtime testing under current user constraint.
